semantic_changes: No production logic is replaced or patched; the case adds a constructor parameter for the configuration id and uses only public API calls.

scope.description: Adds to the cluster harness a case that starts the configuration listed by a StopSign: three fresh instances (pids 1,2,3) built with configuration_id 2 and empty storage must elect a leader, decide four entries and end with identical decided vectors.
assumptions: The next configuration lists the same pids with configuration_id 2 and no flexible quorum, and its instances are built with the same server settings as the stopped configuration (batch_size 2, election/resend tick timeouts 2/4).
Fresh instances start from empty storage, which is how the captured documentation describes starting the next configuration; the harness does not carry any state across the transition.
Ballot ordering in the captured code ignores configuration_id, so the new instances elect among themselves without interference from the stopped configuration's ballots.
Dev profile with overflow checks enabled.
excluded: The stopped configuration is not part of this case; the transition is exercised by starting the next configuration independently, not by transferring state.
Membership changes (a node present in one configuration and absent in the other) are not exercised: both configurations list the same pids.
Message loss, snapshots and the persistent backend are not applied here.

basis.prefix: The test builds Cluster::with_config(3, 2, 2) - three OmniPaxos instances over fresh shared in-memory storage handles with configuration_id 2 and batch_size 2 - then pump_until a (Leader, Accept) exists, appends TestEntry(0..4) on that leader, pump_until every node reports decided_idx 4, and emits case_result_next_config with the configuration id, the leader-found flag, the decided flag and a vector-equality flag. The other four cases of the harness (stale-decided recovery, batched mixed proposals, leader change plus recovery, stopsign reconfiguration) run unchanged in the same target.
basis.responsibility: Under test is the participant set's ability to leave the stopped configuration and form the next one, i.e. that the configuration id carried in ballots and messages does not prevent the new instances from electing a leader and deciding entries.

comparisons.description: Instances of the configuration named by the StopSign elect a leader among themselves.
The next configuration decides its entries, ending with identical decided vectors on every node.
